source_reading: M. Takesaki, Theory of Operator Algebras II, XII.5.13-5.17, printed pp.427-431; original diagrams of the present lessons, no source illustrations used.
visual_check: All final PNGs inspected; matching-plot tick labels adjusted and re-inspected.

figures.caption: The shared refinement has trace masses 1, 1/2, 3/2. The a-coefficients are 3/5,1/5,1/5 and the b-coefficients are 1/2,1/2,1/6. Both positive functionals have mass one. Matching the band projections yields exact orbit distance 1/10+3/20+1/20=3/10; the two shaded areas compute the same value.
figures.assumptions: Type II factor with a finite projection of trace 3 under the chosen trace. All displayed steps and band traces are exact; no finite-dimensional interpretation of half-integer projection traces is intended.

figures.caption: Type I eigenvalues 3/4,1/4 give integer-valued counting-trace tails. In a II1 factor with normalized trace, the quantile mu(s)=1/(2 sqrt(s)), 0<s<1, gives an unbounded positive density of trace one with tail min(1,1/(4t^2)). Its exact mass beyond t=4 is 1/16. The full domain is the squared spectral-integral domain in SO23.
figures.assumptions: Left: type I standard trace. Right: type II1 normalized trace and the trace flag constructed in Section 6. The right curve is a numerical sample of the displayed exact formula; no tail mass is omitted from the stated integral.

figures.caption: Nested nonzero finite-trace projections e<=f give exactly 2(1-tau(e)/tau(f)). The points at ratios 1/n give the finite matrix diameters. Arbitrarily small rank ratios in type I infinity, and trace ratios in a diffuse finite type II corner, give supremum 2. The open endpoint does not claim attainment.
figures.assumptions: States associated with densities e/tau(e), f/tau(f), with 0<tau(e)<=tau(f)<infinity. The smooth line samples the exact distance formula; displayed matrix values are exact.
